The inputs set a compare value to control counting speed, and the bottom 8 bits of the counter are output on bidirectional pins. The documentation appears to be copied from a template and does not match the title. It is likely that the actual neuron implementation is missing or undocumented.
results.summary: This project is titled Hodgkin-Huxley Chip Design, but the documentation describes a clock divider and binary-to-decimal counter driving a 7-segment display, with no mention of neuron behavior. The inputs set a 24-bit compare value that controls counting speed, and the bottom 8 bits of the counter are output on bidirectional pins. With all inputs zero the compare is 10,000,000, giving one increment per second at 10 MHz. The documentation does not match the title, so the actual neuron implementation is unclear.
